newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech analysts expect new floating crown to fall.
newsitem.headline: Czech analysts expect new floating crown to fall.

text.p: Czech market analysts said that the central bank's move late on Monday to effectively float the Czech crown would lead to a sharp fall in the currency when trading resumes to full strength on Tuesday.

"I think in the morning the koruna (crown) will open drastically down," Vladimir Kreidl, economist at Prague's Patria Finance told Reuters. "I think it will find its support level at 15 percent below the current level."

Earlier Czech National Bank (CNB) governor Josef Tosovsky announced that as of Tuesday the central bank would eliminate its fluctuation band against the central parity point of a mark/dollar basket, effectively floating the currency.
He said that the crown would still have some relationship to the mark, but declined to say what that would be.

The crown showed little immediate reaction on currency markets, remaining around -2.0 percent against the basket's central parity level in the hour following the announcement which was made just after 7.30 p.m. (1730 gmt) with British and U.S. markets closed for a holiday.
Floating the crown was the best of several alternatives amid heavy downward pressure on foreign exchange markets, analysts said.
"Given that they couldn't hold the band, this is by far the best alternative," said David Lubin, emerging markets analyst with HSBC Midland bank in London.

Traders have estimated that the central bank has used several billions of dollars to defend the Czech currency over the past 10 days as a huge current account deficit and political instability made the crown a juicy target.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said after Tosovsky's statement that the interventions were becoming too expensive.

Lubin said that other alternatives such as establishing a new central parity mark against the crown's dollar/mark basket, or changing the size of the fluctation band would have "just presented new targets to the foreign exchange markets."
